description: I'm building a prototype for astronaut health monitoring. It uses simulated sensor data to distinguish possible sensor faults from changes in heart rate recovery and suggest what to measure next.
summary: Crew Health Monitor is a Rust prototype that helps a crew decide what to measure next when onboard sensor readings are ambiguous. It uses simulated heart rate recovery data to distinguish a possible sensor fault from a sustained change, including cases where both occur. The prototype selects follow-up checks based on how much uncertainty they can reduce within a limited measurement budget. Interactive scenarios and a reproducible benchmark demonstrate the approach.
details:
The prototype runs locally in Rust and Axum. Its Bayesian model tracks a possible sustained shift in heart rate recovery and a possible sensor artifact. After each simulated observation it updates both probabilities. It ranks available follow-up checks by expected information gain per unit of measurement budget. The crew can review the evidence and see when the data are insufficient.

In a reproducible benchmark of 300 synthetic episodes, 150 contained a sustained shift. The adaptive policy detected 109 of those episodes, compared with 112 when running every available check. It spent 1,488 instead of 5,022 simulation budget units and generated 60 instead of 36 false signals. The measurements, model parameters, and costs are demonstration values. The software has been evaluated on simulated scenarios.

NASA’s Exploration Medical Capability concept of operations informed the design for onboard decision support under communication delays. OpenAI Codex helped implement and test the Rust code and generate synthetic scenarios and benchmark data.
dataRefs: NASA Exploration Medical Capability: Clinical Decision Support System Concept of Operations
projectRefs: OpenAI Codex (implementation, testing, and synthetic data)
